audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate strings (`spikes[2].text`, `mid`, `late` context, `whys[4]`, `wants.foe[1]`) say Defiant Dance (W) blocks Mel's burst and heals Irelia through Radiant Volley.
audit.why: Riot's text for Defiant Dance: 'She takes reduced PHYSICAL damage during the charge.' It reduces physical damage only and it does not heal at all. Mel is a pure magic-damage champion — Radiant Volley, Solar Snare and Golden Eclipse all pass through Defiant Dance at full value. The heal in Irelia's kit belongs to Bladesurge (Q), not W. This is the most consequential error in the entry: it tells a Mel player her level-6 all-in cannot work when in fact W is the one Irelia button that does nothing to her.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance mitigates physical damage and heals nothing, so it is dead weight against Mel — the moment Irelia charges W she has stopped moving and stopped threatening you. Her sustain is Bladesurge's heal, which is what Grievous Wounds answers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vanguard's Edge (R) is described only as part of a 'Sheen/Trinity' power spike; its wall is never mentioned.
audit.why: Vanguard's Edge fires blades that then form a wall which damages and slows anything crossing it. Mel has no dash anywhere in her kit, so the wall is not chip damage to her — it is a hard boundary between her and safety, placed behind her at 125/105/85s. This is the interaction that decides whether Flash is held for damage or for the wall.
audit.corrected: Hold Flash for the Vanguard's Edge wall, not for the burst — with no dash, the wall is what actually kills you.

audit.whatIsWrong: full `breakdown.cooldowns` names Flawless Duet as matchup-defining but gives no number, and never mentions the Bladesurge reset that is the actual gap-close engine.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s — a genuinely long window at rank 1. Bladesurge is 10/9/8/7/6s but its cooldown REFRESHES whenever the target is Marked or dies, which is why a big wave lets Irelia chain to Mel for free. Both numbers are already on disk in the kit file and neither is used.
audit.corrected: Flawless Duet 16s at rank 1 is the countable window; Bladesurge resets on a Marked target or a kill, so wave size, not its cooldown, sets how far she can reach.

audit.whatIsWrong: full `phases[0].side` gives level 1 to Irelia while its own `why` on the same row reads 'Q volleys win every level-1 range war'.
audit.why: The side and the reason contradict each other inside one row. The content layer gives level 1 to Mel, which the kit supports: Bladesurge is 600 range and needs a unit to dash to, while Radiant Volley is 950 and Solar Snare 1000. Level 1 Irelia cannot reach a Mel who respects 600.
audit.corrected: Level 1 is Mel's; the rest of the chart stays with Irelia.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer's content text asks for Grievous Wounds despite the entry repeatedly saying Irelia heals through the poke.
audit.why: Bladesurge heals Irelia on every cast and its cooldown refreshes off Marked targets, so in a big wave she can heal repeatedly during a single trade. Anti-heal timing is what decides whether Mel's chip sticks.
audit.corrected: Name Grievous Wounds against the Bladesurge heal.

audit.why: 33.33% over 9 games is carried consistently and matches the HARD 8/10 grade in the full layer and the Irelia-heavy content chart. No elo-tier language present.

notes: The full layer calls Irelia 'he/him' in tldr, enemyWin, wave, feeding and elsewhere while the content layer correctly uses she/her — same champion-agnostic template seen on other Mel entries, better fixed at the generator than string by string. The single phases[0].side edit is a short enum label ('Irelia' -> 'Mel') and cannot satisfy the +/-10% band; it is recorded in the audit above so the finding survives if the applier rejects it.
